title: Ordinary scalar-extension tensor comparison commutes with first-variable shifts
statement: Let R,A,B,C be commutative rings, A and B R-algebras and C an algebra over A tensor_R B. Use tensor and coefficient conventions from [def-pc-localized-tensor-comparison-property]. Let F be termwise extension from A to C. For A-complexes U,Q, a C-complex N, an integer n and a complex map t:F(Q) to N, put f=mu_F(U,Q)^(-1) then F(U) tensor t and fV=mu_F(U[-n],Q)^(-1) then F(U[-n]) tensor t. Let eK:F(U[-n] tensor Q) to F(U tensor Q)[-n] be F applied to the first-variable tensor shift followed by scalar-extension shift. Let eT:F(U[-n]) tensor N to (F(U) tensor N)[-n] be scalar-extension shift tensored with N, followed by first-variable tensor shift. Then fV followed by eT equals eK followed by f[-n]. This is a square of ordinary complex maps and uses no derived tensor cohomology model.

source.place: Tag 0BYJ; first-variable tensor shift in Tag 0DJA(1)

proof.text: Take the flip in the first complex variable of mapBifunctorComparisonNatTrans for the oplax monoidal scalar-extension map. Compose it with the tensor natural transformation induced by t. The upstream commShift_mapBifunctorComparisonNatTrans_flipApp and Mathlib tensor shift instances make the composite commute with shifts. NatTrans.shift_app_comm at U and -n gives the square; identify its components with the inverse monoidal comparison and tensoring by t.

theorem localizedTensorComparison_shift_transport
    (U Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} C) ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    let F := (extendScalars.{u, u, u}
      ((algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C).comp (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B)))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)
    ∀ (t : F.obj Q ⟶ N),
    let eK := F.mapIso (CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₁Iso U Q
      (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (-n)) ≪≫ (F.commShiftIso (-n)).app (U ⊗ Q)
    let eT := tensorIso ((F.commShiftIso (-n)).app U) (Iso.refl N) ≪≫
      CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₁Iso (F.obj U) N
        (curriedTensor (ModuleCat.{u} C)) (-n)
    (Functor.Monoidal.μIso F (U⟦-n⟧) Q).inv ≫ (F.obj (U⟦-n⟧) ◁ t) ≫ eT.hom =
      eK.hom ≫ ((Functor.Monoidal.μIso F U Q).inv ≫ (F.obj U ◁ t))⟦-n⟧'
